newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF's Marchelli says early parity comment best.
newsitem.headline: BoF's Marchelli says early parity comment best.

text.p: Bank of France council member Paul Marchelli said on Friday a way of avoiding any speculation about what rate European currencies will join the euro would be to make some announcement in April or May 1998.

Speaking in an interview on LCI television, Marchelli said, "If for example in April or in May 1998 the countries which are going to form the euro decide the entry parities in some form...in my opinion that would sort out quite a few problems."

European monetary affairs Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy said in the interview the decision about parties would be formally taken on January 1, 1999, but while premature to say what methods would be used or when some sort of announcement would be made it should be before that date.
"We are not going to wait until (Jan 1, 1999) to allow uncertainty to develop," de Silguy said.
Both de Silguy and Marchelli said they did not think the decisions when eventually announced would take financial markets by surprise.
